about-hero-body: A Bible for those you do life with. Read and study Scripture together, online, on any device, in dozens of languages.
about-playlist-body: Gather passages, links, and videos into a path through Scripture to walk through or share.
about-sessions-body: Read live with your group, wherever each of you is. Everyone follows along in their heart language.

about-content-body: Highlight what speaks to you and write down what you're learning. Your friends' notes show up right in the passage too.
about-mission-body: We believe access to God's Word should stay simple and dependable. Seed Bible is free forever, with no ads, no paywall, and nothing between you and Scripture.

apocrypha-info-text: None of the writings in this section were ever considered Scripture by early Jewish or Christian communities. The Bible is a specific collection of books. Jews and Christians have always agreed on the Old Testament, which comes from a fixed set of sacred writings the Jewish people called the Tanakh and Christians call the Old Testament. The content of the Tanakh and the Old Testament are exactly the same, but are commonly arranged differently. Christians additionally recognize the New Testament, which tells the story of Jesus, his teachings, and the writings of his followers. The writings below were known and widely read at the time the Bible was written, but they were never treated as Scripture. While ancient authors sometimes quoted a wide range of texts including poets, philosophers, and other writings, quoting something is not the same as treating it as Scripture. These writings are included here for historical and literary reference only.

interpretations-intro: Where this translation had to decide how to read a verse, the record says which questions it faced, what it chose or kept open, the alternatives, and the writings behind each. Documented interpretations within a declared corpus — never all possible ones, never a score.
writings-intro: Not only related Scripture: the writings of the book's own period, the copies that carry it, what was written about it later, and the commentary on its verses — each dated, each saying how it relates. Listed because a record names the passage; never all that exist.
